run.note: best_ade_m is the run's own validation on its synthetic corpus, not a measurement on our flights

head: linear 128->256
gelu (measured, see below)

auxiliary.behavior_head: linear 128->19, training only, not used at inference

head_activation_measurement.why: head.0 and head.3 are the two Linear layers; the activation between them leaves no tensor, and effective_config.yaml does not name it
head_activation_measurement.how: at the delivered scale, so only the activation varied: 360 windows from 6 of our own 5 Hz UAM flight runs, scored two ways - the 15 s displacement error against what each flight did, and a continuity residual (how far the first predicted point sits from carrying the last second's observed velocity forward one step, which does not depend on our flights resembling its training motion)
head_activation_measurement.reading: gelu is lowest on both, and the two measures agree. gelu and silu are close because the functions are close; relu and tanh are ruled out by a wide margin. This is strong evidence, not the trained configuration - if the run's own head activation can be sent, it should replace this.

measured_on_our_flights.reading: on our own flights the model is worse than carrying the last velocity forward. That is not a verdict on the model: our flight runs are kinematic and straight-legged by construction, which is the case a constant-velocity rule is exactly right for, while the model was trained on a synthetic corpus of turning, climbing and transitioning VTOL motion where its own validation ADE is 18.8 m. It is worth watching once the twin carries motion that is not straight.

scale_check.why: to see whether the delivered scale is credible rather than to fit one
scale_check.reading: the curve is shallow between 300 and 430 and the delivered 406.93 sits inside it. The delivered value is used as delivered - the delivery note is explicit that the scale is a property of the training run and must not be refitted per input.
